title: MIC comparison uses timing-variant == operator
description:
File: rust/lichen-schc/src/fragment.rs
Line: 963

Issue: The MIC comparison uses == which is not constant-time:
  if compute_mic(&self.storage[..packet_len]) == self.all1_mic

Severity: Low (P3) - CRC-32 is not cryptographic, so timing attacks cannot be exploited for authentication bypass. However, this sets a bad pattern.

What goes wrong: If this pattern is copied to code using cryptographic MACs, it creates a timing side-channel vulnerability. The == operator short-circuits on first byte difference.

Suggested fix: Add a comment explaining why constant-time is not needed here:
  // NOTE: CRC-32 is not cryptographic; constant-time comparison unnecessary

Alternative: Mark as opinion/wontfix since CRC-32 timing is not exploitable. The real fix is the SECURITY comment on compute_mic clarifying CRC-32 is not for authentication.
